definition: In this context, limited responsibility means staff seeing people with mental health conditions as not really belonging in the emergency department and therefore taking only partial ownership of their care. It reflects a reduced sense of duty to assess and manage these patients compared with other emergency patients.

reasons: The packet supports that staff saw patients with mental illness as inappropriate ED users and assumed limited responsibility, but it does not support the added contrast that this was less than for other emergency patients.
The phrase “not really belonging in the emergency department” is stronger and more specific than the packet’s wording and is not directly supported.

The packet supports that staff assumed “limited responsibility” for patients with mental illness and viewed them as inappropriate ED users, but it does not explicitly support that this means patients are “not really belonging in the emergency department,” nor that staff take “partial ownership” of their care.

The definition claims a “reduced sense of duty to assess and manage these patients compared with other emergency patients,” but the packet does not provide this specific comparison or an explicit duty/assessment/management reduction wording.
